title: Quotient factors and canonical coefficient computation coordinates
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^{n+1})$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, and let $q_{m,n}:A_m\to A_n$ be the quotient factor for $n\leq m$ [def-coef-compact-support-reduction-maps]. Then $q_{n,n}=1$ and $q_{m,n}q_{r,m}=q_{r,n}$ for $n\leq m\leq r$. For a scheme $W$, on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the identity and composition isomorphisms for derived coefficient restriction are the canonical sectionwise identity comparisons, with these quotient equalities inserted [def-coef-scalar-restriction-identity, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For a complex $P$ over the completed integral ring sheaf, write $P_n$ for termwise ordinary extension along its level-$n$ projection. Its comparison $L_n(QP)\to QP_n$ is the universal derived counit, conjugated by the homotopy/cochain localization comparisons [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. A pure section $s\otimes x$ is $s$ times the ordinary adjunction unit at $x$. The module-section specification factors its identical equations through generic reducible quotient and balancing section-formula abbreviations, avoiding repeated concrete carrier conversions. No construction chooses objects from existence alone.
